The state of exception expires on 14 November and is likely to be extended or followed by a renewed curfew. Operation Muralla may provoke retaliation by Comandos de la Frontera against security forces in Orellana and Sucumbios, where the group has already ambushed soldiers. Over 90 days, expect further US-supported operations against Los Lobos, Los Choneros and border groups, prison unrest, and attacks on judges, prison staff and local officials after high-value arrests.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 9 Oct — Lima: Lima and Callao transport unions ruled out a strike for now and met senior police commanders at the Interior Ministry to coordinate measures against the attacks.
12 Oct — Cercado de Lima: An informal combi driver was shot in the neck in front of his wife and baby and is in serious condition. Police are investigating it as an extortion case.

13–14 Oct — San Juan de Lurigancho, Lima: Colectivo driver Jean Pierre Rodriguez Hinostroza (23), of the 'Los Pitufos' company, was shot dead by a gunman posing as a passenger. The next day the company received a letter signed 'Plata o Plomo' giving it 24 hours to comply or 'there will be another death'.

13 Oct — Lima: A court ordered 18 months' pretrial detention for three men linked to the 'Los Mexicanos' gang, accused of killing minivan driver Jose Herrera in September by setting the vehicle on fire with him inside.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Extortion networks continue to kill and wound transport workers weekly in Lima and Callao and openly threaten further killings. This is recurring deadly violence by organised criminal groups, though there is no territorial loss of state control. Transport unions have chosen cooperation with the police over a strike for now, which lowers the short-term risk of disruption, but another high-profile killing could reverse that quickly. The 60-day state of emergency declared on 28 August expires around 26–27 October and is very likely to be renewed, possibly with a larger military role under President Fujimori's push to treat extortion gangs as terrorists. Over 90 days, expect continued weekly killings of drivers, intermittent strike threats, and election-related threats ahead of regional polls. Upgrade triggers include attacks on candidates or officials, a mass-casualty extortion bombing, or violent clashes during a strike.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 9 Oct — Santa Cruz: President Rodrigo Paz said road blockades would not be permitted and police and military forces are deployed to prevent them. The government challenged Evo Morales to 'step aside' and ruled out reversing the diesel price rise, which is tied to IMF commitments.

12 Oct — La Paz department and Potosi: Police and the armed forces set up checks at nine access points to La Paz under the 'Bolivia Unida' plan, searching for weapons, explosives and dynamite. Campesino and civic groups in Potosi threatened mobilisations against the diesel decree.
13 Oct — Cochabamba/La Paz: Morales-aligned leaders postponed indefinitely their planned march on La Paz, saying a date would be set with the campesino confederation and Cochabamba coca growers.
15 Oct — La Paz department: Police reported all roads open with no blockades, while keeping forces deployed at the nine strategic points.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Unrest over the removal of the diesel subsidy remains limited to threats, marches and sectoral strikes, without blockades, clashes or casualties. The postponement of the 13 October march shows that the state of exception (to 17 December) and visible police and military deployment are deterring escalation for now. Over the next 90 days, the risk is concentrated on Morales-aligned coca growers in Cochabamba, Potosi campesinos and Santa Cruz civic demands for fiscal redistribution. Any attempt to cut roads will meet the government's stated willingness to clear them by force, which could quickly produce casualties. Return to HIGH if multi-day blockades resume, clearances cause deaths, or protests turn into calls for President Paz's resignation as in May–June.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 9–11 Oct — Nationwide/border: The General Directorate of Migration detained 3,894 undocumented people in operations with the army and police. Dajabon (647) and Elias Pina led the border provinces.

11 Oct — Comendador, Elias Pina: Local deputy Millys Martinez was handcuffed during a police operation. The National Police director and the deputy declared the matter 'resolved' on 15 October, but the internal investigation's results have not been published.

14 Oct (reported) — Distrito Nacional: A man known as 'Lucifer' was shot dead in an alleged confrontation with a Dicrim police patrol. Videos circulating on social media sparked debate over the police account.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. There was no organised armed or political violence this week. Activity was limited to large-scale migration enforcement, routine anti-crime operations and isolated controversy over police conduct. Over the next 90 days, expect deportations to continue at roughly a thousand a day and border-wall construction to proceed. With Haiti's elections postponed and gang reprisals in Artibonite and the Centre, there is a risk of new displacement toward Dajabon and Elias Pina. The Dominican Republic will remain a cocaine transit point with joint US maritime interdictions. The main risks are diplomatic and humanitarian friction with Haiti and scrutiny of police killings, not internal instability.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 9 Oct — Kidd Lane, Kingston 13: Kimesha Gibson (39) was shot, and Lashea Ellis (30) and one-year-old Khael Daley died, after gunmen set fire to their home. A 19-year-old from the community was charged with three counts of murder, arson and firearm offences on 15 October.

13 Oct — Kingston: A former police constable was sentenced to 22 years for the murder of D'Jonnay Graham, and two officers were charged after INDECOM investigations. This followed the 8 October murder charge against a corporal over a 2025 fatal shooting in Granville, St James.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Violence remains criminal rather than organised political or armed-group violence, and murders are on course for a historic low (about 407 by early October, down 24%). The Kidd Lane triple murder and arson is an isolated if brutal criminal case, for which a suspect was quickly charged. The main tension remains the high rate of killings by security forces, with 231 so far this year. The cluster of police convictions and charges this week shows INDECOM accountability is working, but it may also feed friction between police and communities. Over 90 days, expect further contested police shootings, localized roadblock protests and rights criticism. Watch for any escalation into sustained unrest in Kingston/St Andrew or the western parishes, and for late-season hurricane impacts.
